items.title: DEBATE
items.text: Five roles on one Claude model. The moderator frames, proposer and critic argue, the judge rules. Max 3 rounds by default.

items.title: RESEARCH
items.text: Proposer and critic search the live web with Tavily, up to 4 tool calls per turn. Sources appear as inline links.

items.title: TRACE
items.text: Every call goes to LangSmith and Langfuse at the same time. Same run, two UIs. Tool errors stay visible.

panels.title: ONE LOOP, UNTIL THE JUDGE STOPS IT
panels.caption: The judge loops the graph until a verdict. The max_rounds cap (3) is defence in depth.

panels.title: ABOUT · A MULTI-ROLE DEBATE AGENT, TRACED TWICE
panels.text: **lab-debater** runs a structured, Oxford-Union-style debate about any topic you give it. Five roles share one Claude model. Two of them search the live web for evidence. Every call lands in two trace UIs. It is a learning playground. The agents do not know that.

items.text: Five roles share one **Claude Sonnet 4.6** model. Each role has its own system prompt and temperature.
Opens with a sharp focus question, then distils each round into agreement, disagreement and a sharper follow-up.
The proposer argues for, the critic argues against. Both engage the other side directly. Both have research tools.
Up to `MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 4` calls to `tavily_search` / `tavily_extract`, then prose. Sources appear inline as `[claim](https://url)` links.
Ends each round: continue, or emit a verdict. An optional `max_rounds` cap (default 3) is defence in depth.
The full transcript, a `VERDICT:` line, and both trace URLs. An excerpt is in `docs/REFERENCE.md`.

rows.text: [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com). One full debate costs about $0.10-0.20 on Sonnet 4.6 with tools, about $0.05 without.
[cloud.langfuse.com](https://cloud.langfuse.com) (EU) or [us.cloud.langfuse.com](https://us.cloud.langfuse.com) (US). Free tier: 50k observations per month.
[tavily.com](https://tavily.com). Free tier: 1,000 credits per month, one credit per basic search or extract. One debate budgets at most 24 calls, so 40+ debates fit.

panels.title: FULL SETUP · PYTHON 3.13+
lines: # Python 3.13+ (ideally via uv, pyenv, or a PyCharm venv)
# edit .env and paste in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, LANGSMITH_API_KEY,
# Leave the other fields as-is. main.py fails fast if a required key is missing.
$ python main.py "Should remote work be the default for knowledge workers?"

items.text: `LANGSMITH_TRACING=true` in `.env.example`, plus the Langfuse callback in `main.py` (`build_run_config()`).

Every run sends the topic, all prompts, every model reply and the raw Tavily results, including full page text from `tavily_extract`, to LangSmith and Langfuse. Do not debate anything you would not paste into those dashboards.
Set `LANGSMITH_TRACING=false`.

Scraped pages go back into the model as tool results, so a page can carry instructions aimed at the LLM. Acceptable for a local toy with read-only tools. Keep it in mind before giving the agent tools that act.

panels.title: THE GRAPH · SETUP RUNS FIRST

nodes.title: PROPOSER
nodes.sub: Argues for the motion, engages the critic. Tavily.

nodes.title: CRITIC
nodes.sub: Argues against, steelmans the proposer. Tavily.

nodes.title: MODERATOR
nodes.sub: Distils the round, asks a sharper follow-up.

panels.caption: Judge says continue: loop back to the proposer. Judge gives a verdict: END.

items.text: One LangGraph `StateGraph`, six nodes, one conditional edge. The moderator is one function registered at two positions (`moderator_open`, `moderator_distill`); it branches on `len(transcript) == 0`.
Not in a counter: `verdict: str | None` is the single source of truth. The judge parses its own output to set it. `max_rounds` is defence in depth.
`_run_with_tools()` in `debate/nodes.py`. Moderator, judge and setup stay pure-LLM: they arbitrate structure, not evidence.
Each LLM call carries a `run_name` like `proposer-argument-r1`. ReAct iterations add `-iter0`, `-iter1`, ...
`docs/superpowers/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/`. Full reference: `docs/REFERENCE.md`.
4 results with `title`, `url` and a ~500-char snippet. Usually the first call of a turn.
The full page as clean markdown. For when a snippet is too thin for a proper quote.
Both come from [langchain-tavily](https://pypi.org/project/langchain-tavily/). Retrieval knobs live in `debate/tools.py`: `max_results=4`, `search_depth="basic"`, `include_answer=False`.
The loop forces one clean close with the tools still bound and `tool_choice={"type": "none"}`. Anthropic rejects a history with `tool_use` blocks when no tools are defined.

items.lead: Tool errors do not crash the debate
items.text: They surface as `ToolMessage(content="Tool error: ...")` and stay visible in both tracers. The rate-limit day is not hidden.

panels.title: ENVIRONMENT · .ENV.EXAMPLE DOCUMENTS EVERY KEY AND ITS DEFAULT

rows.text: LangSmith. EU accounts must set the EU endpoint; a wrong region means 403 on `/runs/multipart` uploads.

The 429 guardrail in `debate/rate_limit.py`. It honours the `retry-after` header, backs off exponentially otherwise, and stacks on the Anthropic SDK's own retries (default 2 per call): a long 429 storm costs up to 3 x (`RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES` + 1) requests.
Five system prompts. This is where you iterate most when tuning voice.
Node functions, the model factory, the ReAct loop, `MAX_TOOL_CALLS`.
Thin entry point: env, CLI, graph invocation, printing.

items.text: Edit, run, inspect trace, repeat. Ten documented tweaks (prompts, termination rule, `max_rounds`, `MAX_TOOL_CALLS`, `search_depth="advanced"`, model per role, a new role, tools for the judge) are listed in `docs/REFERENCE.md`.

items.lead: Validation is mostly manual, via traces
items.text: `tests/` holds offline regression tests for the forced-close and judge-cap edge paths and the rate-limit guardrail.
No persistence, no UI, no API (CLI only), no streaming, no tool caching, no cross-turn source dedup, no multi-user sessions.

items.lead: Tools for proposer and critic only (Approach 1)
items.text: Approach 2, the judge as fact-checker with receipts, is mapped in the Tavily design spec, not wired in. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-21-tavily-tool-use-design.md`.
`.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the same pytest on every push and PR.
MIT. Do whatever you want with it.

readme.hero_alt: LAB-DEBATER. Agents argue. You read the trace. Experiment. A LangGraph debate agent: five roles on one Claude model, Tavily web research, two tracers.

code:
# clone, enter
git clone https://github.com/VelimirMueller/lab-debater.git
cd lab-debater

# Python 3.13+ (ideally via uv, pyenv, or a PyCharm venv)
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt

# keys
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env and paste in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, LANGSMITH_API_KEY,
# LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, TAVILY_API_KEY.
# Leave the other fields as-is. main.py will fail fast if any required key is missing.

# run
python main.py "Should remote work be the default for knowledge workers?"
